summary: The article accurately reports on the ITAT ruling regarding capital gains from the transfer of a US entity by an Irish company and correctly explains the role of DTAAs in international taxation. It provides generally sound advice for Indian residents and NRIs.

claims.claim: The Delhi Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) has ruled that capital gains from the transfer of a US entity by an Irish company are not taxable in India.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the Delhi ITAT ruling in the case of FireEye Ireland Limited, stating that capital gains from the transfer of a US entity were not taxable in India under the India-Ireland DTAA.

claims.claim: India has DTAAs with over 90 countries, including Ireland.
claims.note: India has DTAAs with over 90 countries. Some sources state over 85, others over 90, and some even over 94. Ireland is consistently listed as a country with which India has a DTAA.

claims.claim: Article 13 of the India-Ireland DTAA typically specifies how capital gains arising from the alienation of property are to be taxed.
claims.note: Article 13 of the India-Ireland DTAA specifically addresses capital gains and allocates taxing rights based on the type of asset.

claims.claim: When an Indian resident sells shares of a foreign company, the capital gains arising from such a sale are generally taxable in India as per the Income Tax Act, 1961. This is because Indian residents are taxed on their global income.
claims.note: Indian residents are generally taxed on their worldwide income, including capital gains from foreign assets, as per Section 5 of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

claims.claim: For NRIs, the taxability of capital gains in India depends on whether the income accrues or arises in India, or is deemed to accrue or arise in India, as per the Income Tax Act.
claims.note: NRIs are generally taxed in India only on income that accrues or arises in India, or is deemed to accrue or arise in India.

claims.claim: Official information on India's Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements can be found on the Income Tax Department's official website, incometax.gov.in, under the "International Taxation" section.
claims.note: The Income Tax Department's official website, incometax.gov.in, provides information on Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements.

article_title: Income Tax Rules: Capital Gains on US Entity Transfer Not Taxable in India
